children: The Inter-American Development Bank is drawing up a two-year engagement plan for Venezuela focused partly on electricity and social protection, IDB President Ilan Goldfajn said on Monday.

The effort includes missions to Venezuela to examine its macroeconomic framework and data and to estimate investment needs across different sectors, Goldfajn told Reuters in an interview. “We are, of course, reengaging,” he said, adding that the bank was devising an “engagement note” setting out what it could do over the next two years.
Goldfajn said the IDB was not preparing its own debt-sustainability analysis for the country, focusing instead on the macroeconomic outlook and sectoral needs.
He did not say how Venezuela’s arrears to the bank would be cleared or when financing could resume.
